newsitem.title: JAPAN: Sony undergoes shakeup to sharpen U.S. focus.
newsitem.headline: Sony undergoes shakeup to sharpen U.S. focus.

text.p: Sony Corp announced a massive reorganisation on Thursday, saying it had to focus more clearly on the lucrative U.S. market or "we'll miss the bus".
Sony Chairman Norio Oga told reporters that Sony wanted to expand its New York unit, Sony Corp of America, by turning it into a "second headquarters" for the giant Sony group.
"It is getting difficult to control everything from Tokyo," Oga told in a news conference. "We'll miss the bus" by not shifting more management functions to the United States, he said.
Oga also announced plans for Sony to move into emerging high-tech areas such as digital satellite broadcasting.

Sony, which expects record group operating profits of 305 billion yen ($2.56 billion) in the current business year to the end of March, says about 30 percent of its sales now come from the U.S. market, more than any other market.
Japan, at 25 percent, is the second-largest market.
Sony Corp of America also oversees Sony's troubled Hollywood film making unit, Sony Pictures Entertainment, and record unit, Sony Music Entertainment.
"After the management at the film making unit was reshuffled, the outlook has become a bit clearer," Sony president Nobuyuki Idei told the news conference.
But Idei, who will now spend more time in New York, said any future listing of the film-making unit was "just one future business option".
Sony overhauled its Sony Pictures management last year, naming new heads of Sony Pictures and both its subsidiaries, Columbia Pictures and TriStar Pictures.
Sony, traditionally strong in studio broadcasting equipment, also aims to play a bigger role in the sharply expanding digital satellite broadcasting market.
Idei said Sony would set up a group company to pull together its content, television-top boxes and other businesses related to digital broadcasting.
Many analysts expect Sony to become the most powerful electronics maker in the burgeoning multichannel television market, including digital satellite broadcasting and cable television.

"Sony has all the important hard technology required for digital broadcasting, on top of the software," said Katsuhiko Sugiyama, president of business consultant company, Musashi Business Development Co.
Sony also said it would set up a consumer electronics marketing company, Sony Marketing (Japan) Inc, on April 1.
The new company will have eight sales units under its wing, and 1997/98 sales are projected at 480 billion yen ($4.03 billion), Sony said.
Japan's cloudy economic outlook, however, concerns Sony, chairman Oga said. "We expect business conditions in the home market to be very severe this year," he said.
